primary_purpose: Define the future request shape for injecting delays during visual simulation without enabling execution yet.

research_alignment.scope_policy: The dissertation should stay focused on delays and delay propagation. Other perturbations are platform extension points, not the current academic claim.

planned_endpoint.current_behavior: No write endpoint is currently exposed by the read-only API.

simulation_run_id.description: Identifier of the future simulation run receiving the delay event.

event_id.description: Client-generated or server-generated identifier for the injected delay event.

event_type.description: Primary delay type. Current dissertation scope should only rely on travel and service delays.

target_type.description: Operational object affected by the injected delay.

target_id.description: Identifier of the affected technician, task, or route leg.

injected_at_simulation_time_minutes.description: Simulation clock time when the user injects the delay.

delay_minutes.description: Non-negative delay duration added to the affected object.

reason.description: Human-readable reason such as traffic, longer service, blocked access, or customer issue.

replanning_policy_hint.description: Optional future hint for selecting or comparing re-planning policies.

validation_rules: event_type must be travel_delay or service_delay for the current dissertation-oriented experiments.
target_type must be technician, task, or route_leg.
injected_at_simulation_time_minutes must be greater than or equal to zero.
delay_minutes must be greater than or equal to zero.
delay injection must not mutate production data.
delay injection must not execute solvers directly from the browser.
future execution must happen only through a controlled backend job API with validation, audit logging, and explicit run boundaries.
expected_future_effects: Mark the affected technician, task, or route leg as delayed.
Recompute affected arrival and service start estimates.
Track propagated delay across subsequent tasks.
Optionally trigger a re-planning decision depending on the selected policy.
Record stability, cost, and feasibility impacts for later comparison.
quality_requirements: The contract must distinguish travel delay from service delay.
The contract must preserve delay propagation as the narrow dissertation scope.
The contract must keep future platform extensions visible but secondary.
The contract must explicitly mark current execution as disabled.
The contract must include non-negative time and delay requirements.
The contract must define how future re-planning decisions will be audited.
conservative_note: This file is only a read-only planning contract. It does not enable delay injection, simulation execution, solver execution, optimization jobs, or write operations.
